key_insight: The paper shows that visual generators fail not just because of rendering limits, but because their knowledge is bounded by fixed training data. To address this, it introduces a search-augmented way to evolve a model’s knowledge boundary for open-ended image generation.
problem_solved: It tackles the long-tailed, constantly changing nature of user prompts in visual generation—such as new characters, trending entities, and post-cutoff events—that models often hallucinate or invent confidently because they do not know the underlying world facts.
method: Builds SearchGen-20K and SearchGen-Bench with 20,839 prompts across 12 failure categories and 22 domains.
Pairs prompts with pre-executed search results to provide external, up-to-date knowledge beyond the model’s training corpus.
Evaluates how search-assisted agentic visual generation can reduce factual failures in open-ended image creation.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work highlights that improving visual generation requires more than scaling models—it needs external knowledge access for factual grounding. It offers a practical benchmark and direction for building more reliable, real-world image generation systems.

paper_title: Search Beyond What Can Be Taught: Evolving the Knowledge Boundary in Agentic Visual Generation
paper_authors: Haozhe Wang, Weijia Feng, Jinpeng Yu, Che Liu, Ping Nie
